items.title: AMD's new X100 chip lineup puts embedded Ryzen AI 'Strix Halo' into robots
items.excerpt: AMD unveiled its X100 embedded APU lineup, putting Ryzen AI 'Strix Halo' silicon with Zen 5 CPU and RDNA 3.5 GPU cores into robots and other 'physical AI' machines. The chips are pitched as on-device brains for humanoids and edge devices, competing with Intel's Panther Lake and Nvidia's robotics platforms. It marks AMD's push into the emerging market for embedded edge-AI compute powering autonomous hardware.

items.title: Arctic Senza AI 370 review: Strix Point in a stealthy under-desk fanless design
items.excerpt: The Arctic Senza AI 370 is a fanless mini PC built around AMD's Ryzen AI 300-series 'Strix Point' APU with a dedicated NPU for on-device AI workloads. Its silent, under-desk-mountable chassis targets buyers who want local Copilot+-class AI acceleration without noise. The review weighs its NPU-driven capabilities against thermal limits of the passively cooled design.

items.title: New Tesla Optimus rival: Leak reveals first details about BYD's AI robot 'Xiao Di'
items.excerpt: EV giant BYD is reportedly preparing to unveil its own bipedal AI humanoid robot, called Xiao Di, positioning it as a rival to Tesla's Optimus. The robot is expected to make its public debut in August and could soon act as a sales assistant presenting EVs in BYD dealerships. It signals another major manufacturer entering the consumer-facing humanoid robot race.

items.title: BrainCo unveils brain-controlled robot AI platform at WAIC 2026
items.excerpt: At WAIC 2026, BrainCo demonstrated remotely controlling robotic hands, arms and humanoids using only a user's thoughts, via its brain-computer interface (BCI) and a brain-controlled robot AI platform. The system translates neural signals into precise robot manipulation in real time. It points toward hands-free, thought-driven control as an interface layer for AI-powered robots.

items.title: My Life With Looki Is a Harbinger of Always-On Recording Glasses to Come
items.excerpt: CNET's Scott Stein lives with Looki, an almost always-on camera-equipped AI pendant that continuously captures and recalls your day. The wearable embodies the extreme assistive aspirations of memory-logging AI, while surfacing the social discomfort and privacy tension of persistent recording. Stein frames it as a preview of the always-on recording glasses and pendants arriving next.

items.title: Everything announced at Samsung Unpacked 2026: new Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2 with an AI Health Assistant
items.excerpt: At Unpacked 2026 Samsung debuted the Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2, both built around an AI-powered Health Assistant that interprets sleep, heart-rate and blood-oxygen data and flags meaningful variations from your baseline. It marks a shift from watches that merely record health metrics to ones that actively interpret and coach on them.

items.title: Meta Is Rethinking Subscriptions on Its Smart Glasses
items.excerpt: Meta paused plans to paywall Conversation Focus — the on-glasses AI feature that uses the smart glasses' microphones to help wearers hear a conversation more clearly — after user backlash, though it signaled other AI features could still land behind a subscription. The episode highlights the tension over how always-on AI hardware features get monetized.

items.title: Samsung Unveils More Smart Glasses Designs from Gentle Monster & Warby Parker
items.excerpt: Samsung teased a fresh slate of Android XR smart-glasses designs, including new frames from eyewear partners Gentle Monster and Warby Parker. The Gemini-powered glasses, developed jointly with Google, expand the style options ahead of a wider release. The reveal fleshes out Samsung and Google's push to make AI smart glasses look like everyday eyewear.
